styling_rules: Use clear Markdown headings, short paragraphs, compact tables, and meaningful bullets.
Use descriptive Markdown hyperlinks close to the claims they substantiate.
Avoid decorative badges, unsupported confidence scores, authorship percentages, and promotional language.
Do not turn the README into a transcript dump; summarize the evidence and link directly to the original passages.
Preserve the technical and academic meaning of the original Spanish-language exchanges.

fundamental_evidence_policy.principle: Every statement about student participation, AI assistance, methodological decisions, computations, literature review, or Milestone 2 outcomes must be grounded in identifiable conversations, documents, code, or recorded execution evidence.
requirements: Read the underlying conversation passages, not only the contribution summary.
Distinguish recorded student instructions from AI suggestions, AI-generated code, tool execution, and retrospective student explanations.
Identify when an AI recommendation preceded the student's adoption of that recommendation.
Distinguish pre-submission records from later feedback-response or evidence-reconstruction activities.
Do not present a retrospective explanation as independent proof that an action occurred before submission.
Differentiate a student's reported activity outside the chat from an independently observable tool action.
Do not invent missing dialogue, attachments, authorship, dates, executions, or research outcomes.
If an assertion cannot be adequately verified, narrow its wording, label its evidence type, or omit it.
Do not use unsupported statements merely to make either the student's or the AI's contribution appear greater or smaller.
Do not claim that the presence of a transcript proves the student's independent programming, execution, reading, or comprehension.
Do not mistake duplicated message representations or runtime context for independent student instructions.

evidence_types.direct_student_instruction: A recorded student request, decision, technical explanation, or correction.
evidence_types.AI_recommendation: A visible model-generated proposal, interpretation, methodological suggestion, or drafted explanation.
evidence_types.recorded_execution: A tool invocation, code change, command completion, generated artifact, or numerical output visible in the logs.
evidence_types.retrospective_student_statement: A student's later account of work carried out earlier or outside the recorded conversation.
evidence_types.reproduced_evidence: A later verified reconstruction of a result; this does not establish independent pre-submission execution.
evidence_types.unverified: Information not adequately supported by the available archive.

milestone_2_scope.academic_context: Milestone 2 is a review of existing predictive learning work and the formulation of an anticipated contribution. It is not the final model implementation or experimental-results milestone.
must_preserve: The student reviewed existing work related to BattLeDIM/L-Town to identify a meaningful and feasible predictive-learning research opportunity.
The proposed task is forecasting n1 pressure 15 minutes ahead.
The feature selection is motivated by hydraulic relationships and the available SCADA measurements in Area C.
The proposed methodology must remain consistent with the methods and knowledge covered through approximately Week 7.
The modeling comparisons and feature-utility experiments are planned work, not completed predictive experiments.
Do not frame the absence of final model-training results or measured improvement as a failure of Milestone 2.
Do not claim predictive improvement, algorithmic novelty, or worldwide research priority without evidence.
Explain the research gap with appropriately limited language: the proposed experiment was not identified in the reviewed literature, which was not exhaustive.
Preserve the distinction between what was presented in the original Milestone 2 submission and what was clarified or reproduced after the professor's feedback.

required_readme_structure.instructions: Explain why this appendix exists, which questions from the professor's feedback it addresses, and how the evidence is interpreted. Distinguish student direction from AI assistance.
Summarize the ChatGPT and Codex records, conversation index, contribution crosswalk, redaction register, and integrity manifest. Verify all numerical counts using the current repository.
Create the ten numbered subsections defined below. Each must contain narrative analysis and source-level links.

required_readme_structure.instructions: Explain that the literature review informed an anticipated, feasible predictive-learning contribution. Separate completed descriptive analysis from future model experiments.
Summarize the division of responsibilities using only independently identifiable records or clearly labeled retrospective statements.
Preserve all substantive disclosures currently present in the README, including missing ChatGPT reply bodies, Codex snapshot boundaries, redaction categories, and the limits of the recovery.
Preserve the public validation command, the private-original comparison procedure, and the correct interpretation of hashes and validation results.

link_requirements: Link directly to the numbered transcript part and relevant line anchor.
Prefer at least one contemporary student message per activity where available.
Link relevant AI responses separately when they materially contributed to the activity.

Verify every destination against the actual repository.
Never invent a line number, message identifier, source ID, or URL.
If a historical record is incomplete, say so.

Do not assign authorship to the student merely because the student approved an AI proposal.
Do not describe student-directed AI code generation as independently student-written code.
Do not infer that retrospective source verification occurred before the original submission.
Do not misrepresent the student's personal literature-review statement as an independently witnessed reading session.
Do not claim the course's entire-conversation requirement has been conclusively satisfied unless the records genuinely support that conclusion.
Do not manufacture evidence to strengthen responses to the professor.
Do not present proposed forecasting experiments as completed results.
Do not change the text of submitted PDFs or recovered conversations to make them match a later explanation.
Avoid unsupported statements concerning academic-integrity violations or the professor's acceptance of the evidence.
